name: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
one_sentence_pitch: Objective: The objective of this investigation is to better understand the structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity.
plain_summary: Objective: The objective of this investigation is to better understand the structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity. Specific objectives of this investigation were: 1. To investigate the structure of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity to understand the stabilizing mechanisms at the flames base. 2.
objectives: Objective: The objective of this investigation is to better understand the structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity.
Specific objectives of this investigation were: 1.
To investigate the structure of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity to understand the stabilizing mechanisms at the flames base. 2.
Determine the liftoff velocity limits for different fuels and burner diameters. 3.
method: The SLICE apparatus consisted of a fan-driven flow duct, exchangeable burner tubes, and integrated sensors to measure flow rates and temperature. This setup used several fuels such as methane, ethylene, and nitrogen-diluted mixtures. Flames were then manually ignited and observed under controlled coflow air conditions.
main_findings: Improved numerical models for flame behavior lead to more efficient combustion technologies on Earth. 2.
Understanding soot formation aids in designing combustion systems with minimum emissions. 3.
Insights into flame stability and behavior to enhance fire safety. 4.
Findings will inform the development of cleaner, more efficient engines and industrial burners.
safety_relevance: Supports NASA’s prevention pillar of spacecraft fire safety.
